move: IPO track. Confirmatory tech review for a pre-IPO investor: platform scalability, the AI forecasting layer, R&D efficiency since the take-private.
name: Anaplan

signals.title: Thoma Bravo-backed Anaplan moves towards return to public markets

why: Connected-planning SaaS, $10.4bn take-private, 4.3 years in and preparing a return to public markets. A pre-IPO stake or a pre-emptive bid is where TPG's software team has played before.

move: Sell-side process under way, so VDD is spent; the buy-side tech DD for whichever sponsor bids is the work to win.
name: Banking Circle

signals.title: EQT reportedly evaluating selling a majority stake in Banking Circle
EQT and Financial Technology Partners seek buyers for Banking Circle

why: Payments and clearing infrastructure behind Stripe, Nuvei and other fintechs. EQT has Morgan Stanley sounding out buyers at $2–4bn — exactly the financial-infrastructure asset Warburg's new $3bn Financial Sector III fund is sized for.

move: IPO-readiness work is already scoped by the banks. The sponsor-side angle is a pre-IPO stake or a full pre-emption, which needs a marketplace-economics and platform read.
name: Carro

signals.title: Carro explores U.S. IPO for up to $500M

why: Southeast Asia's largest used-car marketplace, SoftBank-backed, exploring a US IPO of up to $500m at ~$3bn with an SGX secondary. A dual-track at that size is where a sponsor pre-empts: Warburg has moved its tech dealmakers to Singapore this month.

move: Watch. If Carro lists, Carsome's path narrows to a sponsor or a strategic, and the DD is unit economics by market.
name: Carsome

signals.title: Carsome raises $30m+ strategic round from HKIC, Gobi, Asia Partners

why: Carro's direct rival across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore. Raised $30m in March from HKIC, Gobi and Asia Partners and is an IPO candidate on Nasdaq or SGX. Whichever of the two does not list first becomes a sponsor target.

move: Watch. A buyer would need the platform-rebuild read: how much of the legacy admin stack has been replaced and what remains.
name: Colonial First State

signals.title: CBA completes sale of 55% of Colonial First State to KKR

why: Australian superannuation and wealth platform, A$1.7bn for KKR's 55% from CBA, standalone since December 2021. Four years and ten months in, with a multi-year platform rebuild as the thesis, it is approaching the point where KKR tests the market or CBA's remaining 45% changes hands.

move: Carve-out just agreed, so a TSA and data-separation plan exist. A whole-company bid would need a product-portfolio and AI-exposure read across the remaining segments.
name: Clarivate

signals.title: Clarivate announces sale of Life Sciences & Healthcare segment for $600 million

why: Scientific, IP and academic information services (Web of Science, Derwent, ProQuest), ~$3bn market cap under its debt. Sold Life Sciences & Healthcare to Altaris for $600m in July under a strategic review — a slimmer core that reads as a take-private candidate. Warburg bought Pharma Intelligence out of Informa on the same logic.

move: Watch. Three merged codebases is the DD: how much consolidation has actually happened and what the AI skills layer is built on.
name: Cornerstone OnDemand

signals.title: Clearlake Capital completes acquisition of Cornerstone OnDemand

why: Learning and talent-management SaaS, $5.2bn take-private, five years in. Clearlake has rolled in SumTotal and Saba and the platform is at the point where a 2021-vintage fund looks for a buyer. HR software with a large installed base suits a buy-and-build owner.

move: Watch. A carve-out brings separation and TSA scoping; the broader question is which units still have standalone product momentum.
name: Cloud Software Group (Citrix + TIBCO)

signals.title: Vista and Elliott complete Citrix take-private, merge with TIBCO as Cloud Software Group

why: Citrix merged with TIBCO under Vista and Elliott, four years in, carrying heavy interest expense and refinancing through 2025-26. Too big for one sponsor whole; a carve-out of a business unit is the realistic entry.

move: Watch. A bid would need a market-by-market platform read; the portfolio runs on several separate stacks.
name: Frontier Digital Ventures

signals.title: 2026 half-year results: record revenue and EBITDA, led by 360 LATAM
AGM 2026: Shaun Di Gregorio steps down

why: Owner-operator of property and auto classifieds across Latin America, MENA and Asia. Small cap, founder-CEO stepped down this year, record EBITDA and a 17% margin. A classifieds portfolio at a sub-scale listing is what EQT paid up for in PropertyGuru.

move: Watch. A buy-and-build at this stage carries an integration question across four acquired stacks.
name: Humanforce

signals.title: Humanforce acquires Emprevo and ShiftMatch amid global expansion

why: Workforce-management SaaS for shift-based employers, built by acquisition under Accel-KKR since 2019 (intelliHR, Emprevo, ShiftMatch in April). Seven years in and still buying, which usually means the owner is assembling the platform it will sell.

move: Watch for a 2027 process. DD is the data-asset read: coverage, refresh cadence, and how defensible the payer integrations are.
name: Inovalon

signals.title: Nordic Capital completes acquisition of Inovalon

why: Healthcare data and analytics for payers and providers, $7.3bn take-private, 4.9 years in — the five-year mark is next month. Healthcare data is TPG's strongest sector and a Nordic Capital fund of that vintage will be planning the exit.

move: A live process with two US sponsors engaged. Buy-side tech DD is being scoped by someone this quarter; the platform's legacy-stack question (Xplan, trading) is the diligence.
name: Iress

signals.title: Blackstone, Thoma Bravo in takeover talks with Australia's Iress
Streamlined Iress core earnings rise amid takeover talks

why: Market data, trading and wealth-platform software across APAC, UK and Canada — the data-plus-fintech shape Warburg bought in Clearwater. In play: Blackstone and Thoma Bravo in early talks after a withdrawn A$10.50 approach, and EQT walked away in 2021. A counter-bid or a consortium seat is the obvious angle.

move: Process launching now. Buy-side tech DD on Worldpanel for whichever sponsor bids — panel infrastructure, data pipelines, the AI story on top of it.
name: Kantar

signals.title: WPP and Bain Capital plan full divestment of Kantar, advisers to be appointed in autumn
Bain Capital and WPP set to split, plan sale of Kantar Worldpanel data unit

why: Market research and consumer data. Bain and WPP have decided on a full sale rather than an IPO, in two stages: Worldpanel (consumer panel data, $5–7bn) first, the insights business after, bankers appointed this autumn. Kantar Media already went to H.I.G. for $1bn. A data asset at seven years in a 2019 vintage fund is the textbook secondary.

move: Pre-IPO growth cheque, so a lighter confirmatory review: credit-decisioning stack, model governance, RBI compliance posture.
name: KreditBee

signals.title: KreditBee raises $280m Series E at $1.5bn, India's second unicorn of 2026

why: Indian consumer-lending platform, $1.5bn after a $280m Series E, preparing an IPO for late 2026 or early 2027. Warburg's India franchise is 30 years old and its last fintech there was Avanse; a pre-IPO round is the usual way in.

move: Watch. A consumer subscription stack with a long legacy; DD is renewal-engine resilience and the AI scam-detection roadmap.
name: McAfee

signals.title: Advent-led consortium completes $14bn acquisition of McAfee

why: Consumer security, $14bn take-private by an Advent-led consortium, 4.6 years in. A consortium that large usually exits by IPO, but a sponsor-to-sponsor deal for a cash-generative subscription business is live if markets stay shut.

move: Live, in the sense that the owners are not natural owners. DD is product viability after a distressed year: churn, roadmap, the AI story versus Qualtrics.
name: Medallia

signals.title: Medallia is just the opening act: PE SaaS deals with $50bn+ in debt at risk

why: Experience-management SaaS. Thoma Bravo handed it to its lenders this year, wiping ~$5.1bn of equity. Lenders do not hold software companies for long; a sponsor buying a de-levered Medallia at a reset basis is the obvious next trade.

move: Sell-side under way. The buy-side DD is cloud migration progress off the desktop base and churn to Xero — a classic SSG product/tech read.
name: MYOB

signals.title: KKR said to seek over $2.7bn for MYOB in talks with ANZ

why: Australia and New Zealand's incumbent SME accounting and payroll platform, ~A$1.6bn when KKR took it private. KKR has been sounding out a sale at over $2.7bn, including talks with ANZ. Seven years in, with the Xero fight defining the equity story, this is an exit the fund needs.

move: Watch. Any carve-out brings a data-separation and TSA scoping question.
name: Nielsen

signals.title: Nielsen completes $16bn sale to Evergreen- and Brookfield-led consortium

why: Audience measurement and data, taken private for $16bn in October 2022 by an Elliott- and Brookfield-led consortium. Four years in with a heavy debt load and a measurement-credibility rebuild behind it. A whole-company secondary is big even for Warburg; a carve-out of a data unit is the more likely door.

move: The DD is the Neo migration itself: how much of the installed base has moved, and whether the AI layer is product or marketing.
name: Nuix

signals.title: Nuix reports strong H1 2026 growth amid Neo platform expansion
Nuix acquires French AI decision platform Linkurious for $35m

why: Investigation and e-discovery software with a defensible data moat, mid-migration to the Neo platform and buying French graph-AI firm Linkurious for $35m. Sub-A$1bn, scarred by its 2021 IPO, and the kind of vertical AI application a sponsor can take private and re-platform.

move: Exit preparation under way. Buy-side DD on a security platform this size: product-line consolidation, AI threat-detection claims, and the debt-service case.
name: Proofpoint

signals.title: Proofpoint explores pre-IPO financing and acquisition strategy for public-market return

why: Email and people-centric security, taken private for $12.3bn, ~$4.7bn of debt, past five years. Thoma Bravo has been exploring pre-IPO financing and acquisitions for a public-market return; a sponsor with KKR's cheque size is the alternative to a difficult IPO.

move: Watch. Any entrant would want a ticketing-platform and contract-retention read before pricing it.
name: TEG (Ticketek)

signals.title: Ticketek owner TEG cuts jobs amid contract losses and restructuring

why: Ticketing and live-entertainment marketplace, bought by Silver Lake for US$1.3bn. Lost the Melbourne Park contract to AXS in April and is cutting jobs; the company denies a sale but the market expects Silver Lake to bring in a strategic investor. Six years in, under pressure, is where a minority or full secondary gets done.

move: No process announced. If one opens, the DD is platform modernisation across four verticals and the Stuff integration.
name: Trade Me

signals.title: Trade Me acquires 50% stake in Stuff Digital
Trade Me private equity owners eyeing sharemarket float

why: New Zealand's dominant classifieds and marketplace (property, motors, jobs, general), bought by Apax for NZ$2.56bn in 2019. Apax was weighing a relisting in 2024 and has not transacted since; it bought half of Stuff Digital in 2025 instead. Seven years in, a secondary to a sponsor who likes network businesses is the alternative to an IPO.

move: No process yet. If a bid lands, the DD question is the acquiring stack's resilience and how real the Thriday AI layer is.
name: Tyro Payments

signals.title: ASX-listed Tyro is buying NAB-backed fintech Thriday
Tyro says proposed takeover bid had insufficient value

why: Australia's largest non-bank merchant acquirer, ~A$1bn, repeatedly approached (Potentia 2023, unnamed parties Aug 2025) and rejected on value. Buying Thriday adds an AI-led SME finance layer. A listed APAC fintech at a discount is the Ingenia playbook in a different sector.

move: Watch for a process in 2027. The DD is desktop-to-cloud migration and whether the AI bookkeeping layer is shipping.
name: Yayoi

signals.title: KKR completes acquisition of Yayoi from ORIX

why: Japan's largest SME accounting software, 2.5m registered users, bought from ORIX for ¥240bn ($2.1bn). KKR is at 4.6 years with a cloud-transition story (Yayoi Next) that is the whole value-creation case. Japan vertical software at this scale has few natural buyers, which is what makes a sponsor-to-sponsor deal likely.

move: Watch. The DD is whether the AI-agent product is holding seat counts or cannibalising them.
name: Zendesk

signals.title: Zendesk taken private: IPO no longer expected

why: Customer-service SaaS, $13.9bn take-private, 3.9 years in. An IPO is no longer expected; the owners will look at a secondary or a strategic. AI agents are rewriting the category, which cuts both ways for the equity story.
